items.rationale: The difference is who owns the control flow: in a workflow the code decides the steps in advance, in an agent the model decides the next step at run time. Option a is tempting because workflows seem simpler, but many workflows call a model. Option b mistakes the number of tools for the difference. Option c treats using tools as what makes an agent, but workflows call tools too.

The code fixes the order and the model only fills in steps, so the code owns the control flow and this is a workflow. Option b treats the number of model calls as the test. Option c treats having a tool as the test. Option d treats the model producing the final text as the test; none of these changes who controls the flow.

The reminder runs the same steps in the same order every time, so code can own them, which is cheaper and more predictable. In a, b and d the next step depends on what the previous step finds, so a model has to choose it. Each is tempting for a learner who thinks that the more important or harder a task sounds, the more it needs an agent, whatever its steps are.

Use a fixed workflow where the steps are known and an agent only where the model must choose them, so bookings stay cheap and predictable and troubleshooting keeps its flexibility. Option b assumes an agent is always the better tool. Option c assumes a workflow can cover open-ended requests by adding steps, but the steps cannot be listed in advance. Option d puts a model in charge of routing even for steps that never change, which spends model calls where code would do.

items.rationale: An agent calls the model to choose each next step, and the growing history is read again each time, so it makes more and larger calls than a workflow with fixed steps. A workflow only calls the model where code says to.

When a step must always happen, in a set order, code should own that order, which makes this part a workflow. Options a and c still rely on the model choosing to comply. Option d adds another model call, which may also skip or misjudge the check, so nothing is guaranteed.
